c.tagline: Singapore's northern gateway town - the Causeway to Malaysia, malls, and waterfront parks.

taxi.fareNote: Metered taxis (ComfortDelGro and others) are reliable; ride-hailing via Grab, Gojek, or TADA is equally common and priced up-front. Cross-border taxis run from Woodlands to Johor Bahru.

emergency.note: 999 reaches the police; 995 is for fire and ambulance emergencies.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_desc: The town's civic and commercial core around Woodlands Square, the large Causeway Point mall, Woods Square, the regional library, and the MRT and bus interchange; the most convenient and walkable base.
An older residential estate west of the center with Marsiling Park, Marsiling Mall, and its own MRT station, sitting right beside the Woodlands Checkpoint and the Causeway to Malaysia.
A quiet eastern residential neighborhood known for the award-winning Kampung Admiralty integrated village, 888 Plaza, and the mangrove-filled Admiralty Park; calm and family-friendly.
The smallest and greenest estate, home to most of Woodlands' private condominiums and landed houses, tucked between Marsiling and the waterfront; a relaxed, upscale residential pocket.

The northern coastal edge along Woodlands Waterfront Park and the Johor Strait, with jetty views of Malaysia, park connectors, Republic Polytechnic, and the future RTS Link terminus at Woodlands North.
lodging: Holiday Inn Express Singapore Clarke Quay

water.note: Singapore tap water is safe and rigorously tested.

transit.hours: MRT trains and buses run roughly 5:30 AM to midnight daily; after midnight, taxis, ride-hailing, and limited night buses fill the gap. The Johor Bahru-Singapore shuttle train and Causeway buses run cross-border on their own schedules.
transit.note: Woodlands is served by five MRT stations across two lines - the North-South Line (Marsiling, Woodlands, Admiralty) and the Thomson-East Coast Line (Woodlands North, Woodlands, Woodlands South) - plus an extensive bus network centred on the underground Woodlands Regional Bus Interchange. Woodlands North is the future terminus of the Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS Link).
transit.pay: Tap a contactless Visa/Mastercard or phone at MRT gates and on buses (SimplyGo), or use a stored-value EZ-Link/SimplyGo card sold at station offices and convenience stores. Fares are distance-based and inexpensive.

bus: Causeway Link and public buses to Johor Bahru (Malaysia)
train: Woodlands Train Checkpoint shuttle to Johor Bahru Sentral (Malaysia)

transit.m: MRT to Woodlands via the Thomson-East Coast / North-South lines (60-75 min, one change)
Airport shuttle to the city, then MRT north to Woodlands

tip.r: Not expected; a 10% service charge is usually already included on restaurant bills.
